text:
You have to come with me tomorrow morning! I’m not even joking. The storm was super loud last night, like the sky was throwing tantrums, but now it’s quiet and cold. We’re going to the fish market right when the sun is waking up. It smells weird here—mostly salty and kind of sharp, like old seaweed mixed with wet dog fur. But in a good way? Maybe.

The boats are all bobbing around, still shaking off raindrops. There are big nets piled on the docks, looking like giant green blankets. Fishermen are yelling at each other, their breath making little white clouds in the air. And the fish! They’re so shiny and silver, lying on ice that’s already melting into puddles. Some look angry, with their mouths open wide, and some just look sleepy.

I think there’s a crab hiding under a bucket. If we go really early, before Mom wakes up, maybe we can see if he’s waving hello. Do you want to bring your flashlight?
